title: How to connect Google Business Profile
text:
What this does

Connecting your Google Business Profile allows SwarmReply to monitor all incoming reviews and post AI-generated replies on your behalf. It uses Google's secure OAuth system — your Google password is never stored by SwarmReply.

Step by step

1
In your dashboard, go to Integrations

2
Click Connect Google Business Profile

3
A Google login window opens — log in with the Google account that manages your business listing

4
Click Allow when Google asks for permission

5
You'll be redirected back to SwarmReply — your location is now connected

✓ SwarmReply requests read access to your reviews and permission to post replies. It cannot edit your business listing or billing information.

Which Google account should I use?

Use the Google account that has Owner or Manager access to your Google Business Profile. If you're not sure which one it is, go to business.google.com and check which account you're logged in with.

Troubleshooting

If the connection fails, the most common reason is that the Google account you logged in with doesn't have access to the Business Profile. Try logging into Google Business Profile directly first to confirm access, then reconnect.

✓ You'll know it worked when Google Business Profile shows Connected on your Integrations page — your latest reviews appear under Reviews within a few minutes.

title: Sending your first review request
text:
The fastest way to get more reviews

Review requests are short, personalised messages sent to customers after a visit or service asking them to leave a review. They work because they ask at the right moment — when the experience is still fresh.

💡 Most businesses get their first new review within an hour of sending their first request. Think of your last happy customer and start there.

Send a single request

1
Go to Grow → Review Requests

2
Click + Send Review Request

3
Enter the customer's name and email or phone number

4
Choose your review destination (Google, Facebook, or Yelp)

5
Click Send

Send in bulk

To send to a list of customers, go to Grow → Import Contacts and upload a CSV file with name, email, and/or phone columns. SwarmReply will import the contacts and you can send to the entire list at once.

Choosing which platform to send to

Each template can be configured to send customers to a specific review platform. Go to Grow → Request Templates to set this per template. If you need Google reviews, set your default to Google. If your Yelp rating needs work, create a separate Yelp template.

✓ You'll know it worked when the request shows a Sent status in Grow, and the customer receives the email or text within a few minutes.

title: Adding the webchat widget to your website
text:
What the webchat widget does

The webchat widget adds a chat bubble to your website. When a visitor clicks it, they enter their name and phone number and send a message. You get notified immediately by email and SMS. The conversation continues via text — meaning you capture their contact details before they leave your site.

Get your embed code

1
Go to Settings → Webchat & AI Agent

2
Scroll to Embed code

3
Click Copy embed code

Add it to your website

Paste the script tag just before the closing </body> tag on every page of your website. It looks like this:

<script
src="https://swarmreply.com/chat-widget.js"
data-token="your-token-here"
></script>

✓ The widget loads asynchronously — it won't slow down your website.

On WordPress

Install the Insert Headers and Footers plugin, paste the code in the Footer Scripts section, and save. The widget appears on every page automatically.

On Squarespace

Go to Settings → Advanced → Code Injection. Paste the code in the Footer section and save.

On Wix

Go to Settings → Advanced → Custom Code. Add the code to the body section and apply to all pages.

✓ You'll know it worked when the chat bubble appears in the corner of your live site (hard-refresh first). Send yourself a test message — it should land in your inbox and ping you by email and SMS.

title: Creating your first SMS campaign
text:
What SMS campaigns are for

SMS campaigns let you send a text message to your entire contact list or a targeted segment — for promotions, seasonal offers, win-back messages, or event announcements. Response rates for SMS are typically 5–10x higher than email.

⚠ Only send to customers who have given you their phone number and a reasonable expectation of receiving texts from your business. See our TCPA compliance guide for details.

Create a campaign

1
Go to Campaigns in the sidebar

2
Click + New Campaign

3
Enter a campaign name (internal only — customers don't see this)

4
Write your message — max 160 characters. Use [name] to personalise with the recipient's first name

5
Choose your audience: All contacts, by tag, or a saved segment

6
Choose Send now or schedule for a specific date and time

7
Review the preview and recipient count, then click Send campaign

Monthly SMS limits

Your account includes a monthly campaign SMS allowance. Your remaining balance is shown at the top of the Campaigns page and in the campaign composer, and it resets on the 1st of each month.

💡 Best practice: always end your message with "Reply STOP to unsubscribe." SwarmReply handles STOP replies automatically.

title: Understanding AI Visibility Monitoring
text:
What is AI Visibility Monitoring?

When someone asks ChatGPT, Gemini, or Claude "best Italian restaurant in Sacramento" — does your business appear in the answer? AI Visibility Monitoring tracks this for you. Every week, SwarmReply queries major AI models with discovery questions about your business and your category, then scores and reports how often you appear and how positively you are described.

Your visibility score

The visibility score (0–100) represents the percentage of queries where your business was mentioned across all AI models monitored. A score of 73 means your business appeared in 73% of all queries run that week. The score is compared to the previous week so you can see if you are trending up or down.

Which AI models are monitored?

SwarmReply monitors the three assistants your customers actually use — ChatGPT, Gemini, and Claude — every week. There's nothing to wire up: the scans run on your behalf, with no API keys to provide.

What queries are run?

The Setup Wizard auto-generates a starting set of queries from your business name, type, and city — a mix of discovery queries ("best restaurants in Sacramento"), direct brand queries ("tell me about Bella's Kitchen"), and comparison queries. You can edit those or add your own — up to 15 queries in total — under Get Found → AI Visibility → ⚙ My Queries.

How do I improve my score?

AI models pull from Google ratings and review volume, Google Business Profile completeness, platform listings across the web, and how often your business name appears in credible online sources. The four most impactful things you can do: keep generating Google reviews, publish Google Posts weekly, keep your listings synced across all platforms, and use your business name and city consistently everywhere.

✓ The AI Visibility page includes a built-in improvement guide tailored to your specific score and missed queries.

title: Connecting Square
text:
What this integration does

When a customer completes a payment in Square, SwarmReply automatically sends them a review request 60 minutes later. Works for restaurants, salons, retail stores, and any business using Square as their point of sale.

✓ SwarmReply requests read-only access to your Square payments and customer profiles. It cannot process refunds or modify transactions.

How to connect Square

1
In your dashboard, go to Integrations

2
Click Connect → next to Square

3
You'll be redirected to Square — log in with your Square account

4
Click Allow to grant SwarmReply read access

5
You'll be redirected back to SwarmReply — Square is now connected

Configuring the delay

By default SwarmReply waits 60 minutes after a completed payment before sending a review request. To change this, go to Integrations → Square → Settings and adjust the delay. We recommend 30–120 minutes for most businesses.

What customer info is used?

SwarmReply fetches the customer's name, email, and phone from their Square customer profile (if available). If the customer has no profile attached to the transaction, no request is sent.

⚠ Make sure your review request template is set up and connected to a platform before enabling the Square integration.

✓ You'll know it worked when Square shows Connected on your Integrations page — the next Square payment sends a review request about 60 minutes later.

title: Connecting HubSpot CRM
text:
What this integration does

When a deal is marked Closed Won in HubSpot, SwarmReply automatically sends a review request to the associated contact 30 minutes later. This is ideal for service businesses, agencies, and any B2B or B2C company using HubSpot to manage their sales pipeline.

How to connect HubSpot

1
Go to Integrations

2
Click Connect → next to HubSpot CRM

3
You'll be redirected to HubSpot — log in and choose your portal

4
Grant SwarmReply access to CRM contacts and deals — click Connect app

5
You'll be redirected back to SwarmReply — the integration is live

Which deals trigger a request?

Only deals moved to the Closed Won stage trigger a review request. Closed Lost, Open, and all other stages are ignored.

What contact details are used?

SwarmReply looks up the contacts associated with the closed deal and uses their email address and phone number from HubSpot. If the deal has no associated contacts, no request is sent.

✓ SwarmReply requests read-only access to your HubSpot CRM. It cannot create, modify, or delete contacts or deals.

✓ You'll know it worked when HubSpot shows Connected on your Integrations page — the next deal you mark Closed Won sends a request about 30 minutes later.

title: Connecting Shopify
text:
What this integration does

When an order is fulfilled in Shopify, SwarmReply sends the customer a review request 2 hours later. This gives them time to receive their order confirmation before being asked for a review.

title: Setting up the Stripe payment trigger
text:
What this does

Since you already use Stripe to pay for SwarmReply, you can optionally enable a review request trigger that fires every time one of your customers pays you via Stripe. No additional OAuth connection is needed — SwarmReply already has the relationship.

⚠ This only works if you are using Stripe to charge your own customers — for example, if you run a service business that invoices through Stripe.

How to enable

1
Go to Integrations

2
Find Stripe Payment Trigger and click Connect →

3
Set your delay (default is 60 minutes) and choose your review request template

4
Click Enable

When does the trigger fire?

The trigger fires when a Stripe invoice.payment_succeeded event is received — meaning a successful charge processed through Stripe. The customer's email and name are pulled from the Stripe charge billing details.

✓ If the customer has no email attached to their Stripe charge, no review request is sent.

title: Zapier integration
text:
What Zapier is

Zapier is a tool that connects the apps you already use and moves information between them automatically — no code required. You build a "Zap": when something happens in one app (a trigger), Zapier performs an action in another. Because it connects to thousands of apps, it's become the universal glue for workflows that don't have a direct, native integration.

Why it can be valuable

For a local business, a Zap removes the copy-paste busywork between your tools and makes things happen the moment they should. A few examples of what people automate:

→
A new 5-star review in SwarmReply posts automatically to your team's Slack channel or a Google Sheet

→
A new customer in a booking or POS app you use becomes a SwarmReply contact, ready for a review request

→
A form submission on your website kicks off a SwarmReply review request a few days later

The real value is reach: Zapier covers the long tail of niche apps that no platform integrates with one by one.

Where SwarmReply stands today

A native Zapier integration — with SwarmReply triggers like "new review" and actions like "send review request" — is on our roadmap, but it isn't live yet. We'd rather ship it properly than half-built.

What already covers most of this

Most of what owners reach for Zapier to build, SwarmReply does natively today:

1
Jobber and the Stripe payment trigger fire review requests automatically when a job is completed or a payment clears

2
Square, HubSpot, Shopify, Mindbody, Calendly, and Acuity sync your customer data in, so contacts are ready to go

3
CSV import brings any list of customers in bulk, from any system

💡 Have a workflow these don't cover? Email hello@swarmreply.com and tell us which apps you'd connect — real requests decide what we integrate next, including where Zapier lands on the list.

title: Importing contacts via CSV
text:
When to use CSV import

Use CSV import when you want to upload a list of existing customers from your PMS, CRM, booking software, or any spreadsheet. This is the fastest way to send review requests to your existing customer base.

Required CSV format

Your CSV file must have a header row with at least one of these columns:

• name (or first_name + last_name)

• email

• phone (for SMS requests)

Example header row: name,email,phone

How to import

1
Go to Grow → Import Contacts

2
Click Upload CSV and select your file

3
Map your CSV columns to the SwarmReply fields

4
Preview the first 5 rows and confirm

5
Choose whether to send review requests immediately or save contacts for later

✓ SwarmReply automatically deduplicates contacts — if the same email or phone already exists, it won't create a duplicate.

⚠ Maximum file size is 10MB. For files larger than this, split into multiple imports.

title: Inviting team members
text:
Roles and permissions

SwarmReply has three team roles:

Admin — Full access including billing, team management, and all settings. Typically the business owner or account holder.

Manager — Full operational access — reviews, inbox, campaigns, analytics. Cannot access billing or invite team members.

Staff — Can view and act on reviews, manage the inbox, send review requests, and view basic analytics. Cannot access billing, campaigns, or settings.

How to invite someone

1
Go to Settings → Team

2
Click Invite team member

3
Enter their email address and choose their role

4
Click Send invite — they'll receive an email with a link to set their password

✓ Invite links expire after 7 days. If a team member hasn't accepted, go to Settings → Team and resend the invite.

Removing a team member

Go to Settings → Team, click the three dots next to the team member, and select Remove. Their access is revoked immediately. Only Admins can remove team members.

✓ You'll know it worked when the person appears in Settings → Team as Pending — they switch to Active once they accept the email invite.

title: Importing contacts from CSV
text:
What this is for

Importing your customer list lets you send review requests in bulk instead of one at a time. Once imported, your contacts appear in Grow → Bulk Send ready to receive a request.

2

4
Match the columns to name, email, and phone, then confirm the import

💡 Email is needed for email requests and phone for SMS requests — include both columns when you can so you're free to use either channel.

After importing

Head to Grow → Bulk Send to send review requests to your imported contacts, or send to individuals from Grow → Review Requests.

✓ You'll know it worked when your contacts appear in Grow → Bulk Send with their names, emails, and phone numbers filled in.

title: Choosing your review platform
text:
Where should your reviews go?

SwarmReply can send customers to Google, Yelp, or Facebook. Which buttons your customers see is controlled by the review links you've saved in Settings → Review Links.

Our recommendation: Google first

For most local businesses, Google reviews matter most. They power your Google Business Profile rating, influence local search ranking, and are what most customers check before calling you. If you only set up one platform, make it Google.

When to add Yelp and Facebook

Add Yelp if your industry lives there (restaurants, home services, beauty) and Facebook if your customers already engage with your page. Once you paste those links into Settings → Review Links, they automatically appear as options in your request templates and on the thank-you screen your survey promoters see.

✓ You can offer all three at once — customers simply pick the platform they already have an account on, which removes friction and gets you more reviews.

title: Sending review requests via SMS
text:
Email or text — your choice

Every request template has a channel: email or SMS. Text messages get opened faster — most are read within minutes — which makes SMS a great choice when you ask right after the service.

Setting up an SMS request

1
Go to Grow → Request Templates and create a new template

2
Choose SMS as the channel

3
Write a short message — your review link is added automatically

4
Send a test to yourself from the builder before using it live

⚠️ Keep SMS requests short and always identify your business by name. Your contact must have a phone number on file, and texting customers requires their consent — see our TCPA compliance guide.

Sending

Pick the SMS template when sending from Review Requests or Bulk Send — everything else works exactly like email requests.

title: Customising review request templates
text:
The template builder

Grow → Request Templates is a side-by-side builder: your settings on the left, a live preview of exactly what your customer receives on the right.

What you can customise

1
Channel — email or SMS

2
Message — the subject and body, written in your voice

3
Brand color & logo — pick your brand color and add a logo URL so the request looks like it came from you, not from software

4
Review platforms — choose which buttons appear (Google, Yelp, Facebook), pulled from your saved review links

Test before you send

Use the test send to deliver the request to your own inbox or phone. What you receive is exactly what customers get.

💡 Short, personal messages win. Two sentences thanking them and asking for a minute of their time will outperform a long pitch every time.

title: Setting up the review widget
text:
Show your reviews on your own website

The Rep Widget displays your star rating and recent reviews directly on your website — social proof exactly where new customers are deciding whether to contact you.

Step by step

1
Go to Settings → Rep Widget

2
Choose how you want it to look for your site

3
Copy the embed snippet and paste it into your website where you want reviews to appear — it works on WordPress, Squarespace, Wix, Shopify, and plain HTML sites

✓ The widget updates automatically as new reviews come in — set it once and forget it.

Where to place it

The homepage and any page where customers make a decision (pricing, booking, contact) are the highest-impact spots.

✓ You'll know it worked when your star rating and recent reviews appear on your site where you pasted the snippet (hard-refresh first).

title: When to send review requests
text:
Timing is everything

The single biggest factor in whether a customer leaves a review is how soon you ask after the experience. Ask within a few hours and the experience is fresh; ask a week later and most people have moved on.

The best windows

1
Same day as the service — ideal for home services, salons, repairs, and appointments

2
Right after payment — the natural "transaction complete" moment

3
After a positive interaction — a compliment in person or a 9–10 survey score is a green light

Automate the timing entirely

Connect Jobber (request sent automatically when a job is marked complete) or the Stripe payment trigger (request sent after a successful payment) from the Integrations page, and the right moment is never missed.

💡 Send during business hours — mid-morning and early evening perform best. Avoid late nights, especially for SMS.

title: Sending review requests in bulk
text:
One send, your whole list

Grow → Bulk Send lets you send a review request to many customers at once — perfect for working through a backlog of past customers or a batch you just imported.

Step by step

1
Import your customers first via Grow → Import Contacts (CSV with name, email, phone)

2
Open Grow → Bulk Send and select the contacts to include

3
Choose the request template to use (email or SMS)

4
Send — each contact gets their own personal review link, and delivery status is tracked per contact

⚠️ Only send to customers who actually used your business. Review platforms penalise review gating and bulk solicitation of strangers — and texting requires consent.

💡 Working through old customers? Batch by recency — last month's customers first, then go further back. Recent experiences convert far better.

title: Setting up your NPS survey
text:
What the survey does

Your NPS survey asks customers one question — "How likely are you to recommend us?" on a 0–10 scale — and then invites every customer to leave a public review, while also giving unhappy ones a private channel to flag problems first.

Step by step

1
Go to Grow → Surveys & NPS

2
Customise the messages — the thank-you shown to promoters, and the two follow-up questions detractors are asked

3
Make sure your review links are saved in Settings → Review Links — that's where 9s and 10s get sent

4
Send it — every review request includes a personal survey link for each customer

✓ By default, 9–10 counts as a promoter, 7–8 as passive, and 0–6 as a detractor — the standard NPS bands.

✓ You'll know it worked when you open your own survey link, enter a 9 or 10, and it sends you straight to your Google review page.

title: How NPS routing works
text:
One score, three paths

When a customer taps a score on your survey, SwarmReply routes them automatically:

9–10
Promoters see your thank-you message and buttons to leave a review on Google, Yelp, or Facebook (whichever links you've saved)

7–8
Passives get a simple thank-you — they're satisfied but not enthusiastic, so we don't push them to review

0–6
Detractors are asked two private follow-up questions first, then are also invited to leave a public review

Why this matters

This is how you grow your public rating ethically: everyone gets the same survey, every customer is invited to share publicly, and unhappy customers also get a private channel to reach you first — giving you the chance to make things right.

title: Setting your promoter destination
text:
Where your review links come from

Every customer who's invited to leave a review sees buttons inviting them to share their experience publicly. Those buttons come straight from Settings → Review Links.

Step by step

1
Go to Settings → Review Links

2
Paste your Google review link — and optionally your Yelp and Facebook review page links

3
Save — customers now see a button for each link you've added

💡 To get your Google review link: search your business on Google, open your Business Profile, click "Ask for reviews", and copy the short link Google gives you.

If you serve multiple locations, each location keeps its own links, so customers always land on the right listing.

title: Sharing your survey link
text:
Every customer gets a personal link

When you send a review request, SwarmReply generates a unique survey link for that customer (it looks like …/review/abc123). The link identifies them, records their score once, and routes them to the right follow-up.

Ways to get the link in front of customers

1
Review requests — every email or SMS request includes the customer's personal link automatically

2
Bulk Send — each contact in the batch gets their own unique link

3
Automations — Jobber and Stripe triggers send the link at exactly the right moment without you lifting a finger

✓ Because each link is unique, your results stay clean: one customer, one response, tied to a real interaction.

title: Handling detractor responses
text:
A detractor is a gift (really)

A customer who scores you 0–6 was probably going to tell someone about their bad experience — the survey makes sure they tell you first, privately, so you can make it right.

What detractors see

After scoring, a detractor sees whatever follow-up questions you've put on the detractor path of your survey (by default: what fell short, and what you'd do better). Then — exactly like every respondent, whatever their score — they're shown a neutral invitation to leave a public review. Reviews are never gated on sentiment: the same option appears for promoters, passives, and detractors alike, and every answer is saved with the response.

Where detractor feedback shows up

You don't have to go hunting for it. When an unhappy response comes in, it lands on your Home dashboard's action queue — showing the customer's name, their score, and a preview of what they actually wrote. From there, click through to Reports → Responses (pre-filtered to detractors) to read every answer, or open Reports → NPS & loyalty to see the reasons and per-question results across all your detractors at once.

What to do when one comes in

1
Respond fast and personally — a same-day call or email from the owner defuses most situations

2
Fix what you can — a refund, redo, or sincere apology often turns a detractor into a loyal customer

3
Look for patterns — if three detractors mention the same thing, that's an operations issue, not a one-off

💡 Turn on negative-feedback alerts in Settings → Account so detractor responses reach your inbox the moment they happen.

title: Webchat appearance settings
text:
Make the chat yours

Once the widget is on your site (see Adding the webchat widget to your website), customise how it greets visitors in Settings → Webchat & AI Agent.

What you can set

1
Greeting title — the headline visitors see when the chat opens

2
Welcome message — the first message in the conversation, written in your voice

3
Business hours — so visitor expectations match when you can actually reply

💡 A specific welcome message ("Hi! Ask us about availability, pricing, or anything else") starts far more conversations than a generic "How can we help?"

Changes apply to the live widget as soon as you save — no need to touch the code on your website again.

title: Setting up the AI chat agent
text:
Your 24/7 first responder

The AI agent answers webchat visitors instantly using the knowledge base you give it — capturing leads at 9pm on a Sunday when you'd otherwise miss them.

Step by step

1
Go to Settings → Webchat & AI Agent

2
Turn the AI agent on

3
Fill in your knowledge base — services, pricing, hours, service area, FAQs (see the knowledge base guide)

4
Test it on your own site: ask the questions your customers actually ask and refine the knowledge base until the answers sound right

✓ When the agent can't answer confidently or the visitor asks for a person, it hands the conversation to you and notifies you — it never bluffs on your behalf.

title: Building your AI knowledge base
text:
The agent only knows what you tell it

The knowledge base in Settings → Webchat & AI Agent is the AI agent's only source of truth about your business. The better it is, the more conversations the agent can finish without you.

What to include

1
Services & pricing — what you do, what it costs (even ranges help: "Most jobs run $150–$400")

2
Hours & service area — when you're open and where you go

3
Your top 10 FAQs — the questions you answer on the phone every week

4
Booking process — how a visitor becomes a customer

⚠️ Keep it current. If your prices or hours change, update the knowledge base the same day — the agent will keep confidently giving the old answer until you do.

title: How handoffs work
text:
AI first, humans when it matters

The AI agent handles the routine questions. When a conversation needs a person, it hands off — and you take over in your Messages inbox.

When a handoff happens

1
The visitor asks for a human

2
The agent isn't confident it can answer correctly

3
The conversation involves something only you can decide — a custom quote, a complaint, a scheduling change

What happens next

You're notified (email, SMS, or both — your choice in webchat settings), the conversation is flagged in Messages, and every handoff is logged so you can review where the agent needed help — which is also your to-do list for improving the knowledge base.

title: Managing your inbox
text:
Every conversation in one place

Messages in your dashboard sidebar is where all webchat conversations live — the ones the AI handled, the ones handed off to you, and everything in between.

Working the inbox

1
Filter by open to see conversations waiting on you

2
Click a conversation to read the full history — including what the AI agent already said

3
Reply right in the thread — the visitor sees it in the chat widget (or by text if the SMS bridge is on)

💡 Speed wins leads. A visitor chatting on your site is comparing you to two competitors in other tabs — replying within minutes is the difference-maker.

title: How the SMS bridge works
text:
Run your webchat from your phone

With the SMS bridge on, webchat doesn't chain you to the dashboard: new visitor messages reach you by text, and your text replies go straight back into the visitor's chat window.

Setting it up

1
Go to Settings → Webchat & AI Agent

2
Turn on SMS notifications and SMS replies, and confirm the phone number to use

3
That's it — next time a lead comes in while you're on a job, just reply to the text

✓ Everything still lands in your Messages inbox too, so the full conversation history stays in one place no matter where you replied from.

title: Webchat notification settings
text:
Never miss a lead

Every webchat conversation is a potential customer. Notifications make sure new chats and handoffs reach you wherever you are.

Your options

1
Email notifications — a message to your chosen address when a new conversation starts or the AI hands off

2
SMS notifications — a text to your phone for the same events (pairs with the SMS bridge so you can reply by text too)

Where to set them

Both live in Settings → Webchat & AI Agent, per location — so the right person gets notified for each location you run.

💡 Running a team? Point email notifications at a shared inbox and SMS at whoever is on duty.

title: Importing contacts for campaigns
text:
Build your campaign audience

SMS campaigns send to contacts in your Campaigns → Contacts list. Import them once and reuse the list for every campaign.

Step by step

1
Export your customers as a .csv from your CRM or spreadsheet (name and mobile number at minimum)

2
Go to Campaigns → Contacts and upload the file

3
Review the preview, match the columns, and confirm

⚠️ Only import people who have agreed to receive texts from your business. Texting without consent violates TCPA rules and carries serious fines — see the TCPA compliance guide before your first campaign.

💡 Anyone who has opted out previously is automatically excluded from sends, even if they appear in a new import.

title: Creating audience segments
text:
Right message, right people

Segments let you group contacts in Campaigns → Segments so each campaign goes to the people it's actually relevant to — which means better response rates and fewer opt-outs.

Segments that work for local businesses

1
Recent customers — served in the last 90 days; great for review requests and referral asks

2
Lapsed customers — haven't been back in 6+ months; perfect for a win-back offer

3
VIPs / repeat customers — first access to promotions and seasonal slots

When you compose a campaign, pick the segment instead of the full list. Smaller, targeted sends also stretch your monthly SMS limit much further.

title: SMS campaign limits
text:
How limits work

Your account includes a monthly SMS campaign allowance. The usage meter at the top of the Campaigns page shows messages used, messages remaining, and how far through the month you are.

The details

1
Every message in a campaign counts toward the limit — a campaign to 500 contacts uses 500 messages

2
The allowance resets at the start of each billing month

3
If a campaign would exceed your remaining allowance, trim the audience with a segment or wait for the reset

💡 Consistently hitting the ceiling? The usage meter shows exactly where you stand, and a tighter, well-segmented audience stretches your allowance much further.

title: TCPA compliance guide
text:
The rules of texting customers

The TCPA (Telephone Consumer Protection Act) is the US law governing marketing texts. Violations can cost $500–$1,500 per message, so this is worth five minutes of your time.

The essentials

1
Get consent first. Customers must agree to receive texts from you — a checkbox at booking, a signed form, or a verbal yes you record. Buying phone lists is never OK.

2
Identify yourself. Every message should make clear which business it's from.

3
Honor opt-outs instantly. SwarmReply processes STOP replies automatically and blocks future sends to that number — you never have to manage this manually.

4
Text at reasonable hours. Stay inside 8am–9pm in the customer's local time.

⚠️ This guide is practical information, not legal advice. If you run large campaigns or operate in multiple states, a quick consultation with an attorney is smart insurance.

title: Managing opt-outs
text:
Opt-outs are handled for you

When a contact replies STOP (or STOPALL, UNSUBSCRIBE, CANCEL, END, QUIT), SwarmReply automatically marks them as opted out and excludes them from every future campaign. There is nothing you need to do — and no way to accidentally text them again.

Opting back in

If a customer changes their mind, they can reply START, YES, or UNSTOP to the same number and they'll be re-subscribed automatically.

Why this protects you

Honoring opt-outs immediately is a legal requirement under the TCPA, not a courtesy. Because it's enforced automatically at the sending level, an opted-out contact stays excluded even if they show up again in a fresh CSV import.

✓ A few opt-outs per campaign is normal. A spike usually means the audience was too broad or the message wasn't relevant — tighten your segment next time.

title: SMS campaign best practices
text:
What separates great campaigns from spam

1
Lead with value. A real offer, useful reminder, or genuine update — if you'd be annoyed receiving it, don't send it.

2
Keep it under 160 characters where you can. One message, one idea, one clear action.

3
Identify yourself in the first few words — "Hi, it's Maria from Sunrise Plumbing…"

4
Send mid-morning or early evening, never late at night.

5
Respect frequency. One or two campaigns a month keeps your list healthy; weekly blasts burn it down.

6
Segment. A win-back offer to lapsed customers and a VIP early-access text will both outperform one generic blast to everyone.

💡 Track results per campaign and double down on what your audience actually responds to — your customers will tell you what they want by what they click.

title: How listings sync will work
text:
Coming to SwarmReply

Listings sync is in development. When it launches, SwarmReply will push your business name, address, phone, and hours to the major directories from one place — and flag mismatches that confuse customers and hurt local search ranking.

What to do today

1
Keep your Google Business Profile complete and current at business.google.com — it's the listing that matters most by far

2
Make sure your name, address, and phone are written identically everywhere they appear (your website, Google, Yelp, Facebook)

💡 Consistent business details across the web is one of the strongest local SEO signals — it's worth an hour to audit yours manually while sync is on the way.

title: Fixing a listing mismatch
text:
Why mismatches matter

If your phone number is different on Google than on Yelp, or your old address still appears somewhere, customers get confused and search engines trust your listings less. Automated mismatch detection is part of the listings sync feature currently in development.

How to fix mismatches manually today

1
Write down your canonical details: exact business name, address, phone, website, hours

2
Check the big four — Google Business Profile, Yelp, Facebook, Apple Maps — and correct anything that differs

3
Search your business name and fix stragglers (old directories, chamber of commerce pages) as you find them

✓ Moved or changed numbers recently? Old details linger for years — this audit is especially worth doing.

title: Getting listed on Apple Maps
text:
Why Apple Maps matters

Roughly half of US smartphones are iPhones, and Apple Maps is their default navigation. If your listing is missing or wrong, those customers literally can't find you. Apple Maps will be part of SwarmReply listings sync when it launches; here's how to get listed today.

Step by step

1
Go to businessconnect.apple.com and sign in with an Apple ID

2
Search for your business — it may already exist from public data. Claim it, or add it new

3
Verify ownership (Apple typically calls your business phone)

4
Complete your profile with the same details you use on Google — identical name, address, and phone

title: Getting listed on Bing Places
text:
Ten minutes, free visibility

Bing powers search for Microsoft Edge, Windows, and increasingly AI assistants — a meaningful slice of local searches that most of your competitors ignore. Bing Places will be part of SwarmReply listings sync when it launches; claiming it manually today takes about ten minutes.

Step by step

1
Go to bingplaces.com and sign in with a Microsoft account

2
Use "Import from Google Business Profile" — Bing copies your existing Google listing, which keeps details consistent automatically

3
Verify your business and you're done

💡 The Google import option is the whole trick — never re-type your details by hand when you can sync them.

title: Reports dashboard overview
text:
Your reputation, measured

Reports in the sidebar is your analytics hub. Everything on the Analytics tab is computed from your real data — reviews, requests, surveys, and campaigns — with no estimates or filler.

What you'll find

1
Review overview & trends — total reviews, average rating, the star-by-star distribution, and how rating, volume, and sentiment move over time

2
NPS & loyalty — your NPS score, the promoter / passive / detractor split, the reasons detractors give, and a results chart for every question on your survey

3
Responses — browse individual survey responses, filter by sentiment, channel, date, or keyword, read every answer, and export the filtered set to a spreadsheet

4
Requests & campaigns — review requests sent, plus the results of your SMS campaigns

💡 Use the range picker (7 days / 30 days / 90 days / 12 months) to zoom between "how's this week going" and "how's this year going".

For more on the survey reports, see Reading your NPS & loyalty report and Filtering & exporting survey responses. Competitor tracking, listing accuracy, and Google Posts analytics are coming to Reports soon.

title: Reading your NPS & loyalty report
text:
The loyalty picture, at a glance

Open Reports → NPS & loyalty for everything your surveys are telling you. Set the date range at the top of the page — the whole report respects it.

What's on it

1
Your NPS score — the headline number, from −100 to +100, plus how it's changed versus the previous period

2
Promoters · passives · detractors — how your responses split across the three groups, with counts

3
Top reasons detractors gave — the themes behind low scores, ranked

4
Survey question results — a chart for every question on your survey: choice questions broken down by option, rating and scale questions by value with an average

💡 Open-text answers aren't charted here — they're individual by nature. Read them one by one in Reports → Responses.

Your NPS score also appears on your Home dashboard, so you can keep an eye on it without opening Reports.

title: Filtering & exporting survey responses
text:
Every response, on your terms

The Reports → Responses view lets you dig into individual survey responses instead of just the totals — useful when you want to find a specific customer, audit a recurring theme, or pull data into a spreadsheet.

Filtering

1
Sentiment — show only promoters, passives, or detractors

2
Channel — email or SMS

3
Date range — last 30 / 90 days, 12 months, or all time

4
Keyword — search the text of every answer for a word or phrase (try "wait", "refund", or "rude")

Reading & exporting

Click any row to expand it and read every answer that response gave. Hit Export CSV to download the filtered set as a spreadsheet — one row per response, one column per question — ready for Excel, Google Sheets, or your own analysis.

💡 Filters and export work together: narrow to "detractors who mentioned 'booking' in the last 90 days," then export exactly that set.

title: Understanding your sentiment score
text:
How sentiment is calculated

Sentiment groups your reviews by star rating: 4–5 stars count as positive, 3 stars as neutral, and 1–2 stars as negative. The sentiment trend in Reports shows how that mix shifts week by week over the last 8 weeks.

How to read it

1
Steady and mostly positive — healthy; keep the review requests flowing

2
A negative spike in one week — something specific happened; read that week's reviews and find the common thread

3
A slow slide — a process or staffing issue creeping in; your detractor survey feedback usually names it

💡 Sentiment moves before your average rating does — a 4.8 with two bad weeks of sentiment is an early warning your overall score hasn't shown yet.

title: Using the keyword tracker
text:
Know where you rank

Rank Tracking (under Get Found in the sidebar) follows where your business appears in search results for the keywords that matter — "plumber near me", "best salon in Auburn", whatever your customers actually type.

Setting it up

1
Open Get Found and switch to Rank Tracking

2
Add the keywords to track — your Setup Guide can suggest a starter set based on your business type and city

3
Check back over the following weeks to see positions and movement for each keyword

💡 Track 5–15 keywords you'd genuinely want to win, mixing service terms ("water heater repair") with local intent ("near me", your city name). More isn't better — focused is better.

title: Competitor benchmarking
text:
Coming to Reports

Competitor benchmarking is in development. When it arrives in your Reports dashboard, you'll be able to track competitors' ratings, review volume, and momentum next to your own — so "are we winning?" gets a real answer.

How to benchmark manually today

1
Pick your three closest competitors

2
Once a month, note their Google rating and total review count alongside yours

3
Watch the pace — a competitor adding 20 reviews a month is telling you what consistent review requests can do

💡 The goal isn't to obsess over rivals — it's to know whether your review growth is keeping up with your market.

title: Rating velocity explained
text:
Fresh reviews beat old ones

Rating velocity is the pace of your incoming reviews. Google and customers both weigh recency heavily: a 4.7 with ten reviews this month beats a 4.9 whose last review is from 2024.

Where to see yours

The review volume trend in Reports shows your reviews per week. What you want is a steady drumbeat — not a burst after a campaign followed by months of silence.

How to keep velocity up

1
Make the review request part of every job's closing routine

2
Automate it — the Jobber and Stripe triggers send requests the moment work completes, without anyone remembering to

3
Use Bulk Send occasionally to catch customers who slipped through

title: Your weekly summary email
text:
Your week, delivered

SwarmReply sends a weekly summary email recapping what happened with your reputation — reviews handled, your current average rating, and the highlights worth knowing — so you stay informed without logging in.

Controlling it

1
Go to Settings → Account → Alert preferences

2
Toggle the weekly digest on or off (negative-review and all-review alerts live here too)

Want more detail?

The Reports dashboard has the full picture any time — trends, distributions, NPS, and campaign results across whatever date range you choose.

title: Setting up AI visibility monitoring
text:
Get found by AI, not just Google

Customers increasingly ask ChatGPT, Claude, and Gemini for recommendations — "best electrician near Auburn" — instead of searching. AI Visibility monitoring shows whether those assistants mention you.

Step by step

1
Open Get Found → AI Visibility

2
Add the queries to monitor — the questions a customer would actually ask. Your Setup Guide can suggest a starter set for your business type and area

3
Run a scan — SwarmReply asks ChatGPT, Claude, and Gemini your queries and records whether your business comes up and what's said about it

4
Review the results, then re-scan over time to track your progress

💡 Monitor 5–10 realistic queries. "Best [your service] in [your city]" and "who should I call for [problem]" are the patterns customers actually use.

✓ You'll know it worked when a scan finishes and each query shows a result (mentioned or not), and a visibility score appears. A 0 to start is completely normal.

title: Understanding your visibility score
text:
What the score means

Your visibility score reflects how often the AI assistants — ChatGPT, Claude, and Gemini — mention your business when asked the queries you monitor. Mentioned in most answers: high score. Invisible: low score.

Reading your results

1
Per query — see exactly which questions you show up for and which you don't

2
Per model — assistants differ; you might appear in Gemini (which leans on Google data) but not ChatGPT

3
Over time — re-scans show whether your visibility work is paying off

💡 Don't panic at a low first score — most local businesses are invisible to AI today. That's the opportunity: the bar is low and your competitors aren't watching it.

title: How to improve your AI visibility
text:
What AI assistants actually weigh

AI assistants recommend businesses that look established, well-reviewed, and consistently described across the web. You can influence every one of those signals.

The playbook

1
Grow review volume and recency — reviews are the strongest trust signal AI models lean on. Steady review requests are the engine here

2
Complete your Google Business Profile — categories, services, photos, hours; assistants draw heavily on it

3
Keep your details identical everywhere — same name, address, phone on your site, Google, Yelp, and Facebook

4
Say what you do, in plain words, on your website — pages that literally answer "water heater repair in Auburn" give AI something to cite

5
Re-scan monthly and watch which queries flip from invisible to mentioned

title: Google Posts auto-publisher
text:
Publish straight to your Google Business Profile

SwarmReply posts to your Google Business Profile — offers, updates, and highlights — right from your dashboard, so your profile stays active without logging into Google. Fresh posts are a signal Google rewards, and they surface when customers find you on Search and Maps.

Connect once

1
Go to Settings → Social Posting Accounts and connect Google Business

2
Click Connect and approve access — your locations are detected automatically

Create a post

1
Open Campaigns → Social Posts and select Google Business. You can tick Facebook, Instagram, and LinkedIn at the same time to post everywhere at once

2
Choose a content type and write your update. Google Business posts support text, images, and links (not video or Reels)

3
Post now or schedule it for a date and time — SwarmReply publishes it to your profile for you

💡 Not sure what to post? A short weekly update — a recent job, a seasonal offer, a new service — is plenty to keep your profile looking active and current.

title: Setting up your review links
text:
One setting, used everywhere

Settings → Review Links stores your Google, Yelp, and Facebook review URLs per location. These links power your request templates' platform buttons and the buttons survey promoters see — set them once and everything stays in sync.

Step by step

1
Go to Settings → Review Links and pick the location

2
Google: search your business on Google, open your Business Profile, click "Ask for reviews", and copy the short link

3
Yelp / Facebook (optional): paste the URL of your Yelp listing and your Facebook page's Reviews tab

4

title: Customising AI reply style
text:
Make replies sound like you

SwarmReply drafts an on-brand response to every new Google review automatically. You control the voice in Settings → AI Replies:

1
Tone — warm, professional, casual and more; pick what matches your brand

2

3

Changes apply to every reply drafted from that moment on. New reviews are picked up automatically about every 30 minutes.

💡 Want to sign off on each reply before it posts? Turn on the approval queue — see Editing a reply before it posts.

title: Replies in other languages
text:
Where multi-language stands today

AI replies currently post in English. Language detection is built into the platform, and fully automatic same-language replies are on the near-term roadmap.

Handling non-English reviews now

1
Switch to approval mode (Reviews → Approvals) so non-English reviews wait for you instead of getting an English auto-reply

2
Use Edit on the draft to translate or rewrite it in the reviewer's language, then post

⚠️ If a meaningful share of your reviews come in another language, we recommend approval mode until automatic same-language replies ship.

title: How SwarmReply writes quality replies
text:
What goes into every reply

Replies are drafted by Claude, one of the leading AI models, using your business profile: your business name, type, tone setting, and the specifics of the review itself — the reviewer's name, their star rating, and what they actually wrote. Five-star raves get genuine thanks; critical reviews get a measured, professional response that takes the conversation offline.

Making replies even better

1
Fill in your business details fully in Settings — the more context, the more specific the reply

2
Use Always include for the touches that make replies unmistakably yours

3
Run approval mode for a week when you start — edit anything that misses your voice, then switch to automatic once you trust it

💡 Replying to every review — positive and negative — is one of the strongest signals for both local SEO and AI search visibility.

title: Editing a reply before it posts
text:
Two modes: automatic or approve-first

By default SwarmReply posts AI replies automatically. If you'd rather review each one first, switch to approval mode:

1
Open Reviews → Approvals and set the mode to Approve first

2
New AI drafts now wait in the Approvals queue instead of posting

3
For each draft: Approve posts it to Google as-is, Edit lets you adjust the wording before posting, Reject discards it

The original AI draft is kept in your history even when you edit, so you can always see what was suggested versus what was posted.

💡 Approval mode is per location — a multi-location account can auto-post for one location and approve-first for another.

title: Why can't I send texts yet? (A2P 10DLC)
text:
Texting needs carrier approval first

In the US, every business that texts customers must be registered with the mobile carriers under a program called A2P 10DLC (Application-to-Person, 10-Digit Long Code). It's an anti-spam standard the carriers require — not a SwarmReply rule — and until your registration is approved, outbound texts are held.

What's happening behind the scenes

1
Your business and your messaging campaign are submitted to the carriers for vetting

2
The carriers review and approve — usually a few business days, occasionally longer

3
Once approved, SwarmReply switches texting on automatically — nothing for you to do

What you can do right now

Email review requests work today with no registration required, so you can start collecting reviews immediately while SMS is pending. The moment 10DLC clears, your text and email requests run side by side.

💡 You'll see a banner in Grow and Campaigns while texting is pending — it disappears on its own once you're approved.

title: What number do my texts come from?
text:
A dedicated number for your account

Your review requests and campaigns send from a dedicated 10-digit business number assigned to your account during 10DLC registration. It stays the same, so customers see a consistent sender and can reply.

Replies and STOP

If a customer replies to a text, it's captured so you can follow up. If they reply STOP, they're unsubscribed automatically and won't receive further texts — SwarmReply handles this to keep you compliant.

💡 Always close marketing texts with "Reply STOP to unsubscribe." It's required, and SwarmReply processes the opt-out instantly.

title: Surveys and Google's review policy
text:
The short version

SwarmReply surveys are designed to gather private feedback and to make it easy for happy customers to share their experience publicly. Used as intended, every customer is always free to leave a public review — nothing blocks or filters that.

Why this matters

Google's policies prohibit "review gating" — soliciting public reviews only from customers you expect to be positive while steering unhappy ones away from the public review form. It's worth understanding so you stay on the right side of it.

Using surveys the right way

1
Treat the survey as a feedback tool first — it tells you how customers feel and gives unhappy ones a private way to reach you

2
Keep your public review links available to everyone — in your email signature, on receipts, on your website — not only to survey promoters

3
Never tell a customer they can't or shouldn't leave a public review based on their score

💡 This is general guidance, not legal advice. Review platforms set and update their own policies — when in doubt, check Google's current review guidelines or ask a professional.

title: Reconnecting your Google Business Profile
text:
Why a reconnect is sometimes needed

Google connections use a secure token that can expire or be revoked — for example if you change your Google password, remove SwarmReply's access, or Google times out the session. When that happens, new reviews stop syncing until you reconnect.

How you'll know

If you've turned on the "Google connection breaks" alert (Settings → Account → Alert preferences), you'll get an email or text. You may also see a reconnect prompt on your dashboard.

How to reconnect

1
Go to Integrations in your dashboard

2
Find Google Business Profile and click Reconnect

3
Sign in with the Google account that manages your Business Profile and approve access

4
Syncing resumes automatically — recent reviews catch up within a few minutes

✓ Use the same Google account that owns or manages the Business Profile — a personal account without access to the listing won't work.

title: Webchat isn't showing on my site

text:

The snippet isn't on the page — make sure the embed code from Settings → Webchat & AI Agent is pasted into your site's footer (before the closing body tag) on every page you want it

2

3
Pasted in the wrong place — many site builders need the code in a "custom code" or "footer injection" area, not inside a text block

4

Still not appearing?

Open your site, right-click and choose "View page source," and search for "swarmreply" — if it's not there, the snippet didn't save. If it is there but the bubble doesn't show, an ad-blocker or a conflicting script may be hiding it.

💡 On single-page sites (React, Vue, and similar) the snippet should load once in the main template so it persists as visitors navigate.

Give it a little time

SwarmReply pulls new reviews from Google and Facebook on a regular sync, so a brand-new review can take a short while to appear in your Reviews tab. It isn't instant.

If it still hasn't appeared

title: My visibility score is 0 — what now?
keywords: zero no mentions not appearing not showing score dropped nothing low
text:
A 0 is a starting point, not a failure

A score of 0 means the AI assistants didn't mention your business in this week's test questions — completely normal for a business that's new to AI visibility. The good news: it's the most improvable number on your dashboard, and reviews move it.

What actually moves the score

1
Grow review volume and recency — fresh, frequent reviews are the strongest signal AI models weigh

2
Complete your Google Business Profile — categories, services, hours, photos

3
Keep your name, address, and phone identical everywhere — your site, Google, Yelp, Facebook

4
Say what you do, in plain words, on your website

If your score dropped

Week-to-week movement is normal — AI answers vary, and a competitor's surge can edge you out of a single response. Watch the trend over a few weeks rather than any one scan. Your Overview tab's executive summary explains what changed and what to try next.

💡 Scores build over weeks, not days. Steady review generation is the compounding engine behind a rising score.

title: Data, privacy & security
text:
Where your data lives

SwarmReply runs on established cloud infrastructure in the United States. Your data is encrypted in transit (HTTPS/TLS) and at rest, and access is restricted to the systems that need it.

Payments

All billing is handled by Stripe, a PCI-compliant payment processor. Your card details go straight to Stripe and are never stored on SwarmReply's servers.

Your data is yours

The contacts, reviews, and messages in your account belong to you. SwarmReply uses them only to provide the service — sending the requests you set up, syncing your reviews, and producing your reports. We don't sell your data.

Connected accounts

When you connect Google, Facebook, or another integration, SwarmReply requests only the access it needs and stores the connection securely. You can disconnect any integration at any time from the Integrations page, which revokes that access.

💡 Working on a security or vendor review? Email hello@swarmreply.com and we'll help with your questionnaire.

title: Disputing a fake or unfair review
keywords: remove delete fake bad negative report flag dispute fight respond fraudulent
text:
First, respond — publicly and calmly

Even when a review is unfair, a calm, professional public reply does more good than the review does harm: it shows future customers how you handle problems. SwarmReply can draft a measured response for you to review and post.

If it breaks the platform's rules, flag it

Platforms only remove reviews that violate their policies — spam, conflicts of interest, hate speech, or reviews not based on a real experience. Being negative isn't enough. To report one on Google:

1
Open your Google Business Profile and find the review

2
Use the menu on the review to Report it, and select the policy it violates

3
Google reviews the report — this can take time, and removal isn't guaranteed

The most durable fix

A steady stream of genuine positive reviews outweighs the occasional bad one and pulls your average back up far faster than waiting on a removal. That's the engine SwarmReply is built to run.

💡 SwarmReply can't remove reviews for you — only the platform can — but it helps you respond well and out-earn the bad ones.

title: A payment failed or was declined
keywords: declined failed payment card charge past due billing problem expired
text:
What happens

If a monthly charge fails — an expired card, insufficient funds, or a bank block — Stripe automatically retries it over the following days and emails you. Your account keeps working during this grace period.

How to fix it

1
Go to Settings → Billing and click Manage billing

2
Update your card in the Stripe billing portal

3
Stripe re-attempts the charge — once it clears, you're all set

If it isn't resolved

After repeated failed attempts your account may be paused until payment succeeds. Updating your card and clearing the balance restores access right away, and your data is retained throughout, so nothing is lost.

✓ Card about to expire? Update it ahead of time in Settings → Billing → Manage billing to avoid any interruption.

title: What gets imported when you connect Google
text:
Connecting brings your reviews in automatically

When you connect your Google Business Profile, SwarmReply imports your existing Google reviews so your reputation history is there from day one — no manual entry.

What comes across

1
Your reviews — past Google reviews load into your Reviews tab, and new ones sync automatically going forward

2
Your business details — name, location, and category are detected, so AI visibility and reports are set up for the right business and city

What it doesn't do

Connecting Google does not post anything, change your listing, or message your customers. It reads your profile and reviews so SwarmReply can monitor and help — nothing happens without your say-so.

✓ A large review history can take a few minutes to finish importing on first connect.

title: How soon will I see results?
text:
Reviews — days

This is the fastest win. Once you start sending requests, new reviews typically begin arriving within days, depending on how many customers you reach and how quickly they respond.

AI visibility — weeks

Your visibility score moves as your review volume, recency, and listings improve. Watch the trend over several weekly scans rather than overnight — it's a compounding result, not a switch.

Local rank — weeks to months

Search rankings shift slowly by nature; rank tracking is there to show steady movement over time, not day-to-day noise.

💡 The biggest lever on all three is consistent review generation. Get requests flowing in week one and the rest follows.
